name: Outdoor Pizza Oven Dough
desc: Food-processor pizza dough cold-proofed 1 to 4 days, sized for 12-inch pies in a high-heat outdoor pizza oven.

source.title: Outdoor Pizza Oven Pizza Dough
source.evidence: Same four-ingredient gram formula (535 g high-protein all-purpose flour, 2 g instant yeast, 360 g 40°F water, 12 g Diamond Crystal kosher salt) and the same food-processor method, 75°F dough temperature, and 225 g balls.

ingredients.raw: 535 g high-protein all-purpose flour, such as King Arthur
2 g (1/2 tsp) instant dry yeast, such as SAF
12 g (1 tbsp) Diamond Crystal kosher salt
Extra-virgin olive oil, for oiling the proofing containers and dough balls

steps: Put the flour and yeast in a food processor and pulse 3-4 times to combine.
With the machine running, pour in the cold water and process until a rough ball forms and no dry flour remains, 10-20 seconds. Rest 20 min.

Add the salt on top and process until a mostly smooth ball forms, 20-30 seconds. The dough should read 75°F on an instant-read thermometer; if it is cooler, process in 10-second bursts until it gets there.
Move the dough to a lightly oiled medium bowl, knead once or twice into a smooth ball, cover, and let sit 45 min.
With lightly moistened hands, knead the dough in the bowl until uniform, 5-10 seconds. Cover and leave at room temperature until puffy but not quite doubled, 60-120 min.
On a lightly floured counter, divide into four 225 g pieces (or three 300 g pieces for a 16-inch oven) and shape each into a smooth ball.

Coat each ball lightly with oil and put it in a lidded 4- to 7-inch round container, or on an oiled tray at least 2 inches apart, covered loosely but completely. Refrigerate at least 24 hours and up to 4 days (48 to 72 hours is best).
On baking day, take the balls out of the fridge and leave them covered at room temperature 1-2 hours, until they reach at least 60°F.

Heat the outdoor pizza oven until the stone is fully hot, stretch each ball by hand to 12 inches, top lightly, and bake 60-90 seconds, turning for an even bake, until the rim is puffed and charred in spots.
tips: The cold water is there to offset the heat of the food processor blade; with warmer water the dough overshoots 75°F and ferments too fast.
